sections.title: From ODEs to PDEs: A Visual Shift
sections.content: Briefly review Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) as a 'single-path' relationship. Introduce PDEs as systems with multiple independent variables (space and time). Use an animation showing a line evolving vs. a 2D surface morphing.
sections.example: Comparing a swinging pendulum (ODE - time only) to the vibration of a drum skin (PDE - time and 2D surface coordinates).

sections.title: The Heat Equation: Diffusion in Motion
sections.content: Introduce the Heat Equation as the fundamental PDE for spatial change. Explain the 'concavity' concept—heat flows from hot spots to cold spots. Use a thermal gradient color map animation.
sections.example: A cat sleeping on a cold floor; the heat transfer from the cat's body to the floor tiles over time.

sections.title: The Wave Equation: Ripples and Rhythm
sections.content: Focus on the second-order partial derivative with respect to time. Visualize how a local disturbance (a poke) triggers a wave propagation. Emphasize that speed depends on the medium.
sections.example: A robotic arm striking a guitar string; the animation shows the wave packet traveling back and forth along the string.

sections.title: Boundary and Initial Conditions: Defining the System
sections.content: Explain that PDEs describe 'infinite' possibilities. We need Initial Conditions (snapshot at t=0) and Boundary Conditions (what happens at the edges) to pin down a specific solution.
sections.example: Simulating the water level in an aquarium (PDE) based on the shape of the tank (Boundary) and the initial splash (Initial).

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Impact
sections.content: Synthesize the logic: Variables -> Operators -> Constraints -> Solution. Conclude with how PDEs power weather forecasting and movie special effects.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'fire simulation' in a video game, where PDEs calculate the spread of flames across a 3D environment.
